pr_body:
This patch introduces the ability for a replication job to periodically refresh its physical plan. Here's how replanning works:

- The replication consumer's dist sql planner proposes a new physical plan every 10 minutes, as determined by the new `replication_stream.replan_flow.frequency` setting.

-  it then computes how different the proposed plan is to the current plan. This patch computes difference as the number of _participating_ node changes (addition or removal) in the source and destination clusters as a fraction of the total number of participating nodes in both clusters in the previous plan.

- execute the new plan if this difference metric is greater than 0.1, the default of the new `repliaction_stream.replan_flow.threshold` setting.

In future work, we should consider replanning on data distribution changes, as outlined in #99164.

Fixes #102900

Release note: None

issue_context.title: c2c: implement automatic dist sql replanning on node participation changes
issue_context.body:
If a node gets added to either the producer or consumer clusters during cluster to cluster replication, the dist sql flow of the job should automatically replan and include the new node in the plan. Note that if a node currently in the plan dies, the job already automatically replans via job resumption.


Jira issue: CRDB-27717

@miretskiy You wrote the following in the original PR

> not sure how I feel about fraction here. Almost think that an absolute value might make more sense?  
Like: in a 10 node cluster, you'd need 2 nodes added before replanning. Probably though, even 1 node should be enough?

> Also, consider the fact that in an 11 node cluster, after 1 node was drained (and flow replanned with 10 nodes), you then execute your function, and delta/10 would be 1/10th -- below the threshold. So, you'd never replan in that case (apologies is my math is a bit off -- but you get an idea). I want to make sure  
that drain (and rolling restarts/upgrades) in general are handled appropriately.

> You can do fancy things, and use fraction if <1 and otherwise an absolute value?  
Or you can just use an integer.

My thinking here is that 1) it's ideal to make the setting agnostic to the size of the cluster-- perhaps larger clusters cycle through nodes more frequently; 2) I was following precedent set by related cluster settings `bulkio.restore.replan_flow_threshold`, `changefeed.replan_flow_threshold`, `bulkio.import.replan_flow_threshold`.

I'm inclined to keep this as is, unless you have strong objections?
I'm fine either way -- twas just a suggestion.  Take it or not. up to your or other reviewers.
